Your data never leaves your phone

DollarBlock has no server to keep your data on. No account, no login, no name, email or phone number, and no ad or analytics tracker.

It all stays on your phone: how long you use each app, the limits you set and the receipts for every block and unlock. Not even Google backup takes this data.

The day pass is charged by Google Play. DollarBlock never sees your card — it only gets a "paid".

To erase everything, uninstall the app or clear its data in Android Settings. No copy of ours is left anywhere, because there never was one.
Charged by Google Play. DollarBlock never sees your card.

DollarBlock puts a price on the time you said you didn\'t want to lose. You pick the apps, you set the limits, and past the limit the app locks — unlocking it today costs a day pass. Nothing here is hidden: the app is not a virus, it doesn\'t hijack your phone, and it never forces a payment. You can always choose not to pay, and you can turn off monitoring for any app in the Apps tab whenever you want. We just enforce the deal you made with yourself.
Display only — the day pass is still charged in BRL.

resources.string: This block is not a hijack — it\'s the agreement you made. DollarBlock is not a virus, doesn\'t lock your phone and never forces you to pay: paying is just the shortcut for getting this app back today. You can close this screen and get on with your day, and you can disable monitoring for this app at any time in the Apps tab. We only charge what was agreed — nothing else.

DollarBlock asks for the Accessibility permission for one single purpose: detecting which app you have open in the foreground, so it can show the block screen on top of it once you've hit your own daily limit.

With this permission, the app does NOT read your screen content, does NOT capture text you type, does NOT collect passwords, and does NOT send any data off your device. It only checks which app is currently in front.

You can revoke this permission at any time in Android Settings.
